cards.title: George W. Ivie
cards.body: Executive Director and CEO of the MRC, the non-profit industry association established in 1963 to audit US media measurement. In 2021 the MRC's job was not to recount Nielsen's ratings — nobody could — but to rule on whether Nielsen's methods still met MRC minimum standards. The board's levers were hiatus, suspension, reinstatement.
cards.prompt: An audit finds a number that money is billed against is wrong. Name the power an accreditation body has here, and the one it does not have.
cards.answer: It can rule the method non-compliant and pull accreditation, which changes what the vendor may sell. It cannot state the corrected number — only a system that retained the raw events can produce that.

cards.title: The homes that should have been pulled
cards.body: COVID severely curtailed Nielsen's in-person field visits. Homes that tripped alerts stayed in the sample instead of being withheld. By February 2021 about 9,400 of roughly 40,000 US panel homes carried such alerts, 2,400 of them high priority. MRC put the resulting understatement of Total Usage of Television, persons 18-49, at approximately 2 to 6 percent.
cards.prompt: Nielsen's failure was in the sampling frame, not in the counting. Why does that distinction decide whether the published number can be fixed?
cards.answer: A counting error is fixable — recompute from the retained events. A sampling-frame error means the published figure was never a count, so correcting it means re-running a model under a different assumption about which homes were valid. That yields a range with standard errors, not a value.

cards.title: MRC Statement on Nielsen National Television Viewing Estimates Analysis
cards.body: Four pages you can open today. Panel arithmetic, a February TUT change range of 2.2% to 5.6% averaging 4.8%, and the method in MRC's own words: Nielsen's simulation of February excluding the homes assumed to be impaired. MRC adds that the range, and the originally reported ratings, are alike estimates with standard errors.
cards.prompt: This document reports a percentage range instead of corrected ratings. Which single word in its own description of the method tells you a recount was never available?
cards.answer: Simulation. Nielsen re-ran February with the impaired homes excluded; nothing was recounted from stored records, a different model was run. So the output is an estimate carrying standard errors, not a value an invoice could be rewritten from.

cards.title: Not adjustment factors
cards.body: The Video Advertising Bureau published “Behind Billions of Lost TV Impressions,” treating MRC's percentages as adjustment factors. MRC issued a public correction: it never positioned them that way and did not recommend that use — they were estimates of understatement for the single month of February 2021. An error bar is not a credit note.
cards.prompt: Your ad platform bills from a model rather than a log, and an audit finds you undercounted by 2 to 6 percent. Why can you not simply credit every advertiser 4 percent and close the dispute?
cards.answer: An aggregate directional range with standard errors is not a per-advertiser correction. The error is not spread evenly across ads, dayparts or demographics, and no per-account evidence exists to allocate it. MRC publicly refused exactly that use of its figures.
